creator: Thomas, Julie P.; Reid, Mary L.; Barclay, Robert M. R.; Jung, Thomas S.
citation: Thomas, J., Reid, M., Barclay, R., & Jung, T. (2025). Data from: Influence of reproductive status on occupancy of salvage-logged boreal forest by moose (Alces americanus) [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.bk3j9kdpn
samplingProtocol: Camera traps in salvage-logged (low and high retention) and unsalvaged burned boreal forest stands, June to September; detections summarised per 15-day survey period.
closureNote: one summer season (five 15-day periods), analysed as single-season occupancy
geographicCoverage: Burned and salvage-logged boreal forest (see the paper); no coordinates deposited
temporalCoverage: survey year not stated in the deposit; periods fall in June-September

notShipped.bears: grizzly and black bear detection rate on the same cameras (an index from the same detections)

title: Female moose with and without calves on camera traps at 89 burned boreal forest sites: multi-state detections, five 15-day periods
abstract: Multi-state detections of female moose (0 no female, 1 female without calf, 2 female with calf) per 15-day survey period at 89 camera sites in salvage-logged and unsalvaged burned boreal forest, with stand and landscape covariates and survey month; the any-moose table is thomas_2025_boreal_moose_occ.
notes: State 2 (female with calf) implies a detected female; males are not recorded in this table.

stateCodes.1: female moose detected without a calf
